title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 2 Sep 2026
summary: On 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, where built-up land covers 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 52.5%. No flag applies to this date, and 100.0% of the circle has data.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land is the brightest surface, at 6.07 dB in HH, while the circle averages -1.81 dB in HH and -13.8 dB in HV. The ratio of HV to HH over the circle is -11.99 dB.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land has an HV:HH ratio of -17.15 dB, the lowest of all types, because walls send the pulse straight back in HH. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 59.32 km2, give the strongest land HV, -12.84 dB, from leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields sit at -10.46 dB in HH and -18.71 dB in HV. Changing fields, 4.8%, are at -16.73 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies on this date. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. Possible cause of bright points among the fields: farm buildings and walls; the optical photo would show them.
